Title: How to Fix Missing Virtual Game Cards on Nintendo Switch After Update
IntroLines: Are your virtual game cards missing on your Nintendo Switch after a recent update?
In this video, I'll show you how to deregister console conflicts, clear the cache, and restart to get them back.

Sections.Heading: SOLUTION 1: DEREGISTER CONSOLE IN NINTENDO ESHOP
Steps: •  First, from your HOME Menu, open " Nintendo eShop " from the bottom toolbar.
•  Select the user profile linked to your Nintendo Account.
•  Select your " Profile Icon " in the top-right corner to open Account Information.
•  Scroll down the right panel to locate the " Primary Console " section.
•  Select " Deregister " .
•  Enter your Nintendo Account password if prompted for security.
•  Select " Deregister " again to confirm the console status removal.
•  Now, press the " HOME Button " to exit back to your home screen.
•  Open the " Nintendo eShop " once more to automatically re-sync your account and license status.
•  Finally, return to your HOME Menu and check if your virtual game cards start appearing.
Sections.Bridge: If your virtual game cards are still not showing up, let's clear out corrupted temporary cache data.

Sections.Heading: SOLUTION 2: CLEAR SYSTEM CACHE FOR YOUR USER PROFILE
Steps: •  First, from your HOME Menu, open " System Settings " from the bottom toolbar.
•  Scroll all the way down the left sidebar and select " System " .
•  Scroll to the very bottom on the right side and select " Formatting Options " .
•  Select " Clear Cache " .
•  Choose your primary user profile.
•  Select " Reset " to confirm clearing temporary cache files and saved IDs.
•  Finally, confirm on-screen that the cache data has been successfully deleted.
Sections.Bridge: Now that the cache has been reset, let's perform a full system reboot to reload your game licenses.

Sections.Heading: SOLUTION 3: RESTART YOUR CONSOLE TO RE-INDEX LICENSES
Steps: •  First, press and hold the physical " POWER Button " on the top of your console for three seconds.
•  Select " Power Options " from the menu.
•  Select " Restart " .
•  Wait a few moments for your Nintendo Switch to reboot completely.
•  Ensure your console is connected to the internet to verify your digital rights.
•  Open the " Virtual Game Cards " menu or library from the HOME Menu.
•  Finally, verify that all of your missing virtual game cards have been restored to your screen.

OutroLines: And that's how you can fix missing virtual game cards on your Nintendo Switch after an update.
